Freeport|Bahamas.f: Freeport grew from a 1955 grant of 50,000 acres to Virginia financier Wallace Groves, who held lumber interests on Grand Bahama.

Bonaire|Caribbean Netherlands.f: Bonaire is home to one of only four nesting grounds for the Caribbean flamingo.

Tobago|Trinidad and Tobago.f: Tobago changed hands 33 times, the most in Caribbean history, before the 1814 Treaty of Paris ceded it to Britain.

Cozumel|Mexico.f: Cozumel flourished from about 1250 CE as an important Maya port and pilgrimage centre.

San Salvador (Bahamas)|Bahamas.f: San Salvador is the probable site of Columbus's first landing in the Americas on 12 October 1492, though this is disputed.

St. Croix|U.S. Virgin Is..f: Columbus named a St. Croix site Cabo de la Flecha after the first recorded fight between the Spanish and a New World native population.

Cayo Largo del Sur|Cuba.f: Nobody lives permanently on Cayo Largo, and hotel workers stay about 20 days before returning to families on nearby islands.

Cayo Coco|Cuba.f: Cayo Coco, a setting for Hemingway's Islands in the Stream, is linked to Cuba by a 27 km causeway across the Bay of Dogs.

Nueva Gerona|Cuba.f: Near Nueva Gerona, the Presidio Modelo prison held Fidel and Raul Castro from 1953 to 1955 after the failed Moncada Barracks attack.

Governor's Harbour|Bahamas.f: Founded in 1648 by William Sayle and the Eleutherian Adventurers, it claims to be the start of the post-Lucayan Bahamas.

Abraham's Bay|Bahamas.f: HMS Driver, the first steamship to circumnavigate the globe, was wrecked on Mayaguana on 3 August 1861.

Rock Sound|Bahamas.f: Rock Sound's Ocean Hole is an inland blue hole whose water rises and falls with the ocean tide through underground channels.

Exuma|Bahamas.f: Elizabeth Harbour in Exuma was allegedly a favorite lair of Captain Kidd.

Matthew Town|Bahamas.f: Matthew Town's Morton Salt plant makes a million tonnes of sea salt a year, North America's second largest solar saline operation.

Arthur's Town|Bahamas.f: Bahamian-American actor Sidney Poitier was raised around Arthur's Town on Cat Island.

Treasure Cay|Bahamas.f: Treasure Cay began as Carleton Point, founded in 1783 by about 600 Loyalists fleeing the post-Revolutionary United States.

La Grande Rivière|Canada.f: The Hudson's Bay Company ran a trading post at Big River House on the La Grande River between 1803 and 1824.

Cockburn Town|Turks and Caicos Is..f: The National Museum here holds the Molasses Reef Wreck, dated 1505 and the oldest known European shipwreck in the Americas.

South Caicos|Turks and Caicos Is..f: South Caicos was a major exporter of salt and an important centre of regional trade until the 1960s.

Puvirnituq|Canada.f: Puvirnituq's name means putrefied, said to come from an epidemic that left too few survivors to bury the dead.

Codrington|Antigua and Barb..f: In 1685 Christopher Codrington and his brother John established Codrington as the main residential area on Barbuda.

Marsh Harbour|Bahamas.f: Hurricane Dorian made Category 5 landfall at Marsh Harbour in 2019, tying the Atlantic record for sustained winds at landfall.

North Eleuthera|Bahamas.f: At Glass Window Bridge, a 30 ft strip of rock separates the Atlantic Ocean from the Bight of Eleuthera.

Wabush|Canada.f: Wabush appears as Waknuk in John Wyndham's post-catastrophe novel The Chrysalids.

Fort Simpson|Canada.f: Fort Simpson's coldest recorded temperature is -56.1 C, set on 1 February 1947.

Points North Landing|Canada.f: Points North Landing was founded by Norcanair pilot George Eikle and sits near uranium mines such as Cigar Lake.

Cayman Brac|Cayman Is..f: Brac is a Gaelic word for bluff, and the island is named for The Bluff, a limestone ridge rising 43 meters.

Norman Wells|Canada.f: Oil from Norman Wells was piped to Whitehorse through the wartime Canol Project, with the flow starting in 1944.

Canouan|St. Vin. and Gren..f: Canouan is commonly nicknamed The Billionaire's Island as an exclusive retreat for wealthy people and celebrities.

Watson Lake|Canada.f: The Sign Post Forest was started in 1942 by a homesick US soldier building the Alaska Highway, who posted his home town's name.

Sanirajak|Canada.f: Sanirajak means the shoreline in Inuktitut, and the community began in 1957 with construction of a DEW Line site.

South Bimini|Bahamas.f: A small freshwater well with a plaque marking the Fountain of Youth sits on the road to South Bimini Airport.

Andros|Bahamas.f: Andros has the world's largest collection of blue holes, with 178 on land and at least 50 in the sea.

Sandspit|Canada.f: Sandspit's annual average temperature equals Port Hardy's, which lies almost 3 degrees of latitude farther south.

Kuujjuarapik|Canada.f: Kuujjuarapik's Inuktitut name means little great river.

Stony Rapids|Canada.f: Stony Rapids hit its record low of -50.6 C twice, on 26 January 1966 and again on 13 January 1972.

Cat Island|Bahamas.f: Cat Island has the Bahamas' highest point, Mount Alvernia, formerly Como Hill, rising 63 metres.

San Andros|Bahamas.f: Black Seminoles and slaves reached Andros in 1823 by canoe and 27 sloops to settle Red Bays on the west coast.

Cambridge Bay|Canada.f: Cambridge Bay has never recorded a temperature above freezing between 31 October and 19 April.

Dawson City|Canada.f: The Klondike Gold Rush, begun in 1896, turned a First Nations camp into a city of 16,000 to 17,000 by 1898.
